chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal who said:
I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him about the fermented drink. So he wrote: 'It is the wine and regarding it is a legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker'.

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعِ: A specific type of fermented drink mentioned in hadith

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on the fermented drink known as Fuqqa' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise reply from Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), the specific fermented drink 'al-fuqqa'' is explicitly equated with wine (khamr), thereby triggering the full prescribed legal penalty (hadd). This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the intrinsic nature of the beverage rather than its specific name or preparation method, ensuring that any intoxicant falls under the category of khamr. The decision reflects the broader jurisprudential principle that the defining characteristic of wine is intoxication, regardless of the source of fermentation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal who said,
‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassanasws asking himasws about the fermented drink. So heasws wrote: ‘It is the wine and regarding it is a legal penalty (Hadd) of the wine drinker’.
en.sarwar: 15. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal who has said the following: “
I once wrote to abu al-Hassan and asked about al-Fuqa’. He (the Imam) said in writing, ‘It is wine and the penalty for drinking it is like that for drinking wine.’”
